mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of such tightening episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant after controlling for sector composition.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% signals a broad-based collapse in residential and non-residential demand, which depresses corporate earnings and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong export growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which raises wage growth and input costs, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings growth offsets margin compression in the short term.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of rapid inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average, combined with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a supply-side recovery with tight labor conditions, which boosts earnings expectations and yields positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 6-month MA and UNRATE falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such episodes, or the effect is not robust during periods of high commodity price volatility.
